name: Platinum Agent Console
tag: Build, run and watch a team of business AI agents from one console, with costs and errors in plain view.

scenarios.title: Build a sales support team
scenarios.ask: Set up {agents} agents to handle {leads} inbound leads a week: qualify, research, draft replies and book calls.
steps: Builder
Created {agents} agents from templates: Qualifier, Researcher, Reply writer, Scheduler.
Qualifier
Scores each lead on fit and urgency. In this sample, {=round(leads * 0.35)} of {leads} leads pass.
Researcher
Adds a short company profile to each qualified lead.
Reply writer
Drafts a first reply for review in the console.
Scheduler
Offers call times from your calendar once you approve the reply.
followups: Can I change how leads are scored?
Yes. The Qualifier uses a short rule list you can edit in plain words, like company size or budget mentioned. Changes apply to new leads right away.
What if an agent goes wrong?
Every run is logged with inputs and outputs. You can pause one agent without stopping the rest.
Why does cost depend on lead count?
Each lead uses a few model calls for scoring, research and a draft. The console shows cost per run so you can see where money goes.

scenarios.title: Monitor agent health
scenarios.ask: Our agents run {runs} times a day and about {=errors}% of runs fail. Show me where and why.
steps: Monitor
Grouped {=max(1, round(runs * errors / 100))} failed runs from the last day by agent and error type.
Analyst
About 60% fail on one tool call: the CRM rate limit is hit at the top of each hour.
Fixer
Proposed spreading scheduled runs across the hour and adding a retry with a short wait.
Alerting
Set an alert if failures pass {=round(errors * 1.5, 1)}% in any hour.
followups: Does the console retry failed runs?
Only if you turn on retries for that agent. Retries are limited and logged so a broken agent does not run up costs.
Can it notify us in chat?
Yes. Alerts can go to email or a team chat channel with a link to the failing run.

scenarios.title: Keep costs inside a budget
scenarios.ask: We have a ${=budget} monthly AI budget across {agents} agents. Make sure we stay inside it.
steps: Meter
Tracked spend per agent. Current pace is about ${=round(budget * 1.2)} for the month.
Analyst
Two agents use a large model for simple sorting tasks.
Optimizer
Suggested a smaller model for those two and caching repeat lookups.
Guard
Set a soft cap at 90% of budget that pauses non-urgent agents and asks you first.
followups: Will a cheaper model hurt quality?
For sorting and routing, usually not. The console runs both models on a sample first and shows the results side by side before switching.
What does pausing non-urgent agents mean?
You mark agents as urgent or not. At the soft cap, non-urgent ones wait until you approve more spend or the month resets.
